item.content:encoded:
Got mixed feelings about voting on this. On the one hand, it's a rather unoriginal idea that isn't very well written. On the other hand, it's from the early days of this site and standards were different back then; it's still a fun idea, even if already done. The only reason I'm saying it's badly written is because the writing standards have changed. Judging a 12 year old scip on today's writing standards feels anachronistic and wrong. It's a product of the time and it can't help that.

So while it certainly doesn't earn an upvote, I don't feel right downvoting it.

item.title: I
item.content:encoded:
Maybe his luck only functions in regards to games of chance or life-or-death situations?
There is a blurb that states that if personal are working against him to purposely reduce the chances of success, his ability to succeed is reduced. So maybe the arrest and legal trial were 100% certain, as well as the sentencing was 100% certain through bribery?
The article also doesn't state which games he was winning at prior to his arrest - it may have just been roulette or craps; games that don't have an opposition, where as blackjack or poker may have different results.

Though I do agree that becoming a d-class due to winning too much at a casino is a bit much. Usually they just ask you to leave if a you are unreasonably lucky without proof of cheating (citation needed)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A life sentence for cheating in Vegas!?
And how did they even catch him, given that the probability adjustment is automatic?
Assuming they did catch him, how in the world was he convicted? There couldn't be any admissible evidence because magic. Even the lamest public defender should have gotten the charges thrown out in minutes; and that's before factoring his luck into the trial.
And getting picked out of jail by the Foundation is atrociously unlucky, how did that happen?

Basically, in order to be internally consistent, there needs to be some hint that being a D class in a Foundation cell is (or soon will be) the best possible outcome for him. Looming XK event, outbreak of SCP-### with massive casualties in Nevada, something like that.
